note:
1.4.0 for the wagmi tier. One release forward from 1.3.1, nothing skipped.
Disruption is quiet and neither core floor moves: codex stays at 0.147.0 and
claude at 2.1.227.

The box half, measured on wagmi-claw on 2026-09-02 before this pointer was
written. The claw carries two members and both hold a persistent core at or
above the floor, and the per-task core's companion host is present, so no member
reads as core-moving and this claw's own classifier will not defer the release
to the quiet window. A claw on this channel measures itself the same way before
it rides: one read of the members group, and one look at each member's launcher.

This release installs rails a claw did not have. It seeds /etc/orchestrate.conf
with four settings, adds a swapfile sized to the box and an out-of-memory guard,
installs the memory check and the stall check with their timers, and installs
the wake rail as a system service.

Three things on wagmi-claw are older copies of what this release ships: the
notifier, the wake rail program, and the memory check that is absent there
entirely. The run replaces each one and names it in its own output rather than
converging in silence. The wake rail restarts when it is replaced, and a live
session on the box loses a beat and nothing else.

The two lines /etc/orchestrate.conf seeds once and then keeps, the delegate
model and the permission posture, take this box's current values. A claw that
already carries that file keeps what it has.

The dead-man ping is enrolled per claw from the hub and it is not automatic.
Until it is wired, the memory check says out loud that no check is wired rather
than failing quietly.
